acceptance: A hint shows only after the pointer rests on its control (the native toolkit's half second) and goes as soon as the pointer leaves.
Tooltips and other overlays take the active palette's menu, text and canvas colors through light, dark and Sub Theme changes, at the selected type scale.

reason: Native hints are hover-only: keyboard focus opens none (so there is no Escape dismissal or press-focus rule), a hint shows its label without a shortcut line, and clipped values (such as a long project path) get no overflow-only hint.

TS draws every hint in one document-level layer, so it must strip native title bubbles (including SVG titles) while keeping accessible names, link hints with aria-describedby, remove a hint whose trigger unmounted, honour explicit content only, and suppress hints in editor scopes and menus that draw their own cards. A native control owns its own hint, which goes with it; there are no title bubbles to strip, and editor and menu controls that show their own cards carry no hint.
